answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable bond in a scarce resource, then assign work only after a beacon-selected random audit checks its signal against independently observed outcomes. If several identities coordinate or submit fabricated results, the audit can expose the shared pattern and slash their bonds, while honest agents recover theirs. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up real value for every persona and risks losing it; merely generating more identities on shale-like cheap compute does not buy influence.
